faqs.a: Zalgo text stacks Unicode combining diacritical marks (U+0300-U+036F) on top of normal letters. Each mark merges with the letter before it, which creates the corrupted, glitchy look.
These marks are standard Unicode characters, so they render in most apps and browsers. Some platforms (a few games, old systems) strip combining marks, in which case the text shows up normal.
faqs.q: Will zalgo text work on Discord, Instagram and WhatsApp?

zalgo-text-generator.formula:
seed = FNV-1a(input) XOR (level x 7919) XOR direction flags   (seeded PRNG: mulberry32)
for each character c in input:
  output += c
  if c is whitespace: continue
  if above on:  append `level` random marks from the 52-char UP set (U+0300-U+036F)
  if through on: append `level` random marks from the 15-char MID set
  if below on:  append `level` random marks from the 40-char DOWN set
marks added = letters x level x (directions on)

zalgo-text-generator.workedExample:
Input: "hi" | Chaos level: 2 | All directions on

Step 1: input has 2 letters (h, i), no spaces.
Step 2: marks per letter = 2 above + 2 through + 2 below = 6.
Step 3: total marks = 2 letters x 6 = 12 combining marks.
Step 4: output length = 2 base letters + 12 marks = 14 code units.

So "hi" becomes h + 6 marks + i + 6 marks — the exact marks are picked by the seeded generator, so the same settings always reproduce the same glitch.

At level 10 with all directions on, one letter collects 30 marks: 10 above + 10 through + 10 below.
